data.title: Itaconix plc Earnings Call Signals Rapid Growth Ambitions
data.description:
Itaconix plc ((GB:ITX)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Itaconix plc’s latest earnings call struck a distinctly upbeat tone, as management celebrated record first-half revenue, its first-ever adjusted EBITDA break-even and rapid expansion across key regions. Executives balanced this optimism with a candid view of growing administrative costs, reliance on strong reorder patterns and exposure to concentrated supply chains and tariff volatility.

Record Revenue and First EBITDA Break-Even

Itaconix reported record first-half revenue of $8.3 million, a 72% increase half over half, signaling accelerating demand for its specialty polymers. The company also achieved adjusted EBITDA break-even for the first time, reversing a $200,000 loss in the comparable period and marking an important milestone on its path to sustainable profitability.

Promotion

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Performance Ingredients Drive the Top Line

Performance Ingredients were the primary growth engine, with revenue more than doubling to $6.7 million on the back of higher reorder volumes from existing customers. New customer wins added further momentum, underscoring rising adoption of Itaconix’s plant-based polymers in detergents and related applications.

Gross Profit Growth and Margin Discipline

Gross profit rose 74% to $3 million, while gross margins held steady at 36%, indicating that growth has not come at the expense of pricing. Management credited customers’ willingness to pay for performance and environmental benefits, alongside disciplined pricing strategies that protect profitability.

Regional Growth and EMEA Breakout

The company posted its fourth consecutive period of revenue growth, with North America up about 29% half over half and EMEA soaring 166%. EMEA now accounts for roughly half of group revenue versus about one-third previously, reflecting a long-awaited sales takeoff after years of market development.

Customer Expansion and Reorder Momentum

Much of the revenue surge stemmed from existing customers increasing order volumes as their products gain wider retail distribution and consumer acceptance. Itaconix also added two new major customers, one in North America and one in EMEA, plus around 10 smaller accounts that broaden its commercial base.

New EMEA Anchor Customer Emerging

Management highlighted a newly won EMEA customer with the potential to deliver substantial volumes over time. While reorder rates are still being watched closely, executives expressed strong enthusiasm that the relationship will convert into a fully ramped customer contributing meaningfully to future revenue.

Broader Customer and Geographic Base

Two customers each generated more than $1 million of revenue, together representing about 40% of first-half sales, yet the company is also building a tier of midsize accounts between $500,000 and $1 million. Because many customers are contract manufacturers serving multiple brands, the underlying exposure is more diversified than headline customer numbers suggest.

North American Unit-Dose Expansion

In North America, revenue growth was supported by wider engagement with brands adopting tablets and capsules for detergents. Itaconix expects to reach its near-term goal of 600 million unit-dose pods in 2026, positioning the company squarely in the shift toward convenient, pre-measured formats.

Cash and Working Capital Strength

Cash and investments ended the half at $5.1 million, up from $4.4 million, while working capital stood at about $4.4 million. Management said the company is in a solid cash and working capital position, though it anticipates reinvesting a further $300,000 to $400,000 to support growing inventory needs.

Stratham Facility Underpins Growth

The Stratham, U.S. facility currently provides all the infrastructure needed to meet the medium-term revenue objective of $30 million and beyond. The site is running 24-hour shifts three to four days per week, with flexibility to add operating days as demand expands, limiting near-term capacity constraints.

High Fixed-Asset Turnover and Lean CapEx

The Stratham plant delivered fixed-asset turnover of 15x for the period, which management described as well ahead of industry peers. Most throughput optimizations have been achieved with limited capital expenditure, suggesting an efficient asset base that can scale volumes without heavy spending.

Continuing to Invest While Hitting Break-Even

Despite reaching EBITDA break-even, Itaconix continued to invest in talent, systems, product development, commercial expansion and production capabilities. These investments are designed to support future growth and operating improvements, even as the company tightens its focus on profit generation.

Headcount and Systems to Support Scale

Average headcount increased from about 26 employees to 33, mainly to handle higher manufacturing volumes and to advance new detergent, crop and paint opportunities. An ERP system implementation is underway, with go-live targeted by the end of 2026 and full operational use expected in 2027.

Path to Positive Full-Year EBITDA

Management expects to translate first-half progress into a small positive EBITDA for the full year, despite higher administrative expenses. Clear EBITDA profitability in the second half depends on achieving revenue above $14.8 million and maintaining reasonable reorder rates from recently onboarded customers.

Medium-Term $30 Million Revenue Goal

Executives outlined a plan to reach $30 million in annual revenue within three to four years using existing U.S. operations. Key to this goal are securing one more large EMEA detergent customer and further traction with purpose-driven brands in North American unit-dose detergents.

Longer-Term Ambition to $100 Million

Beyond the medium term, management sketched an ambition to build Itaconix into at least a $100 million business. They see growth coming from deeper penetration in core detergent markets and from emerging product lines in paints and crops as those applications mature.

Breakthrough Dishwashing Tablet

The company has developed and patented an 8-gram dishwashing tablet that needs no plastic wrapper, offers high plant-based content and targets super-premium cleaning performance. Using 7.7 grams less product per dose than the U.S. super-premium leader, Itaconix has already signed a bulk supply agreement with a major brand, though deliveries may be delayed.

Triple-Chamber Pod Innovation

Itaconix also introduced a patented triple-chamber dishwashing pod combining two liquid chambers with one powder chamber. The pod uses 3.3 grams less per dose than the market leader while matching performance, reflecting the company’s intent to deliver efficiency and sustainability alongside cleaning power.

Cold-Wash Laundry Tablet Pipeline

A new 8-gram laundry tablet designed to dissolve in cold wash cycles and provide cleaning and odor control is in late-stage development. Management expects a final formulation within the next couple of months and believes the product could spark brand discussions for a potential launch in the first half of 2027.

Large Detergent Market Still Underpenetrated

The company sees a sizeable opportunity in about 70 billion annual dishwasher cycles across EMEA and North America and slightly beyond. Its plant-based scale inhibitor currently features in less than 4% of those cycles and its odor neutralizer is barely present in laundry, leaving significant room for growth.

Phosphate Replacement Tailwind

Itaconix’s TSI scale-inhibitor polymers are gaining ground as replacements for phosphates, which face increasing bans due to environmental concerns. Management argued that, when properly formulated, these polymers can actually lower overall product cost because less material is needed while maintaining or improving cleaning performance.

Advances in Sustainable Paints

The company is developing a safer class of paints with no volatile emissions, fewer toxic ingredients and higher plant-based content. With patents on its binder and formulation, a trademarked brand name and collaboration with a leading paint company, Itaconix aims to be comfortable with an excellent, no-VOC paint product sometime in 2027.

Crop Trials Point to New Revenue Streams

Field trials are underway on more than 100 acres of row crops across several U.S. states, with firm evaluations expected later this year or early next year. If results on yield and economics are positive, the company plans to expand trials to at least 10,000 acres in the following season, opening another avenue for growth.

Global Commercial Reach and Partnerships

Itaconix’s formulations now appear in products across Asia-Pacific, the Americas and Europe, including foot-odor control in India and fabric sprays in China. Strategic collaborations with Croda in home care and Nouryon in hair styling extend the company’s reach and help embed its polymers into established global supply chains.

Regulatory and IP Strengthening

The company has secured full approval for its copolymers in home care in China and obtained an international cosmetic ingredient listing for sodium polyitaconate. Management emphasized strong patent, know-how and trade-secret coverage, citing a successfully contested European patent that was withdrawn to protect its existing IP.

Supply Chain Risk Management

To mitigate operational risks, Itaconix maintains raw materials on-site and in third-party warehouses, works closely with suppliers to spread inventory, and uses off-site storage for materials and finished goods. Backup equipment for critical plant components further supports resilience, particularly important given its single-facility footprint.

Rising Administrative Expenses

Administrative expenses rose about 49% half over half to around $3.2 million, an increase of roughly $1 million. The jump was driven by added personnel, new product development, transportation costs tied to higher EMEA demand and expanded commercial activities, underscoring the cost of scaling the business.

Early Stage of Profitability

Despite reaching adjusted EBITDA break-even, management stressed that profitability is still in its infancy, with only a small full-year EBITDA expected. Clear profitability in the second half hinges on surpassing $14.8 million in revenue, which requires both solid reorder patterns and ongoing operational execution.

Dependence on Reorders and New Wins

Second-half performance and the march toward $30 million in revenue rely heavily on reasonable reorder rates from newly acquired customers. The plan also assumes one more major detergent win in EMEA and continued progress in North American unit-dose formats, highlighting execution risk around customer conversion and retention.

Single-Source Itaconic Acid Exposure

Itaconic acid, a key raw material, is currently produced only in China, leaving Itaconix dependent on a geographically concentrated supply base. Management expressed comfort with existing suppliers and sees no immediate issue, but investors will note the strategic risk if disruptions or trade tensions intensify.

Shipping Costs and Tariff Volatility

The company is managing fluctuations in shipping costs, tariffs and transit times through selective price increases and temporary surcharges. A small surcharge has been applied to some customers in response to recent tariffs, with management hoping to remove it if trade conditions normalize.

Working Capital Reinvestment Needs

Inventory ended slightly below target because a large customer order shipped at the end of June, but management expects to invest another $300,000 to $400,000 into working capital. This reinvestment aims to ensure sufficient stock to support further growth and smooth out shipment-related lumpiness in reported revenue.

One-Facility Footprint and Expansion Options

Production is currently concentrated at the Stratham facility, and the company is mitigating single-site risk with off-site warehousing and backup equipment. Any future expansion would likely involve a second operation outside the U.S., though timing, location and funding remain to be decided.

Paint Commercialization Still Some Distance Away

Management described the paint opportunity as a deliberate optimization process, acknowledging that commercialization remains several steps away. The goal is to reach confidence in an excellent, fully compliant product by around 2027, meaning meaningful paint revenue is unlikely in the near term.

Crop Results Await Confirmation

While initial crop trial results are encouraging, firm evaluations on yield and economics will only emerge later this year or early next year. Any move to expand to at least 10,000 acres will depend on those findings, leaving the agricultural revenue opportunity as a promising but unproven pipeline.

Pivot Away from Slower Opportunities

Reorders in sustainable leather have proved difficult despite positive initial tests, leading the company to redirect effort toward faster-moving markets. Development of superabsorbent materials is also on hold because the plant-based product is still more expensive without clear performance advantages over fossil-based alternatives.

Limited Focus on Hand Soaps and Gels

Hand soaps and gels are currently a low priority because the company’s ingredients deliver fewer benefits at skin pH than in higher-pH solid detergents. Management does not see sufficient revenue potential in these categories relative to other opportunities, and is concentrating resources elsewhere.

Lumpy Revenue Reporting and Market Dynamics

Shipment timing can cause notable lumpiness in reported revenue, and management therefore does not plan to issue quarterly updates. Instead, Itaconix will communicate progress through announcements and shareholder outreach, while noting that phosphates remain a cheaper alternative in regions where they are still allowed, limiting adoption of non-phosphate formulas.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Growth Outlook

Management’s guidance points to exceeding $14.8 million in second-half 2026 revenue with clear EBITDA profitability and a small positive EBITDA for the full year. Longer term, the company targets 600 million unit-dose pods in North America in 2026, $30 million in revenue within three to four years from existing operations, and eventual scale to at least $100 million as detergents, crops and paints mature.

Itaconix’s earnings call painted the picture of a company moving decisively from niche innovator to scaling specialty-chemicals player, underpinned by record growth and expanding global reach. Investors will watch closely whether reorder volumes, new customer wins and disciplined execution can overcome rising costs and supply-chain risks to deliver on the ambitious revenue and profitability trajectory outlined by management.

data.title: Fever-Tree Drinks PLC Maps Strong Growth Path
data.description:
Fevertree Drinks PLC ((GB:FEVR)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Fever-Tree Drinks PLC struck a distinctly upbeat tone on its latest earnings call, stressing broad-based first-half growth, improving margins and earnings, and powerful momentum in the U.S. market. Management acknowledged a handful of short-term headwinds, including heavier U.S. marketing spend, U.K. on-trade softness and an EPR provision, but sounded confident about delivering a roughly 60% EBITDA uplift over the next two years.

Broad-Based First-Half Growth Across Regions

Brand revenue rose 8% at constant currency, with every major geography contributing. The U.S. grew 11%, Europe 10%, the U.K. returned to growth, and the rest of the world posted solid progress, underscoring the mixer maker’s success in driving global demand despite uneven macro conditions.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Margins, EPS and Profitability Moving Higher

Adjusted EBITDA margin edged up 20 basis points to 10.9%, while normalized EPS grew 5%. EBITDA expanded faster than revenue even after a sharp increase in U.S. marketing investment, highlighting underlying operating leverage as the company scales and tightens cost discipline.

Market Share Gains Against Category and Rivals

Management emphasized continued share gains across key regions, with Fever-Tree outpacing both the wider mixed-drinks category and competitors. These gains suggest the brand’s premium positioning and innovation strategy are resonating with consumers and retailers alike.

Extended Buyback and Strong Cash Generation

Robust cash generation and a solid balance sheet allowed Fever-Tree to extend its share buyback program by another GBP 60 million for 2026. Including the prior GBP 100 million tranche, about GBP 160 million will be returned to investors, reducing shares in issue by roughly 7% over 18 months.

Molson Coors Partnership Driving U.S. Momentum

The tie-up with Molson Coors is beginning to deliver, with broader distribution, better shelf visibility and stronger in-store execution. Fever-Tree launched its first national U.S. marketing campaign and achieved record retail value share in both tonic and ginger beer, underlining growing brand traction.

Accelerating U.S. Off-Trade Sales Growth

Off-trade sales in the U.S. accelerated from 6% growth in Q1 to 11% in Q2 and 16% through July and August. Management said the uptrend reflects more retail doors, expanded shelf space and improving rate of sale, reinforcing confidence in sustained U.S. growth.

U.S. Distribution Expansion and Local Production

Fever-Tree is widening its U.S. reach beyond tier-one bars into more mainstream tier-two accounts, while boosting execution and in-store presence. Onshoring cans, alongside existing local glass production, means more than half of U.S. volumes should be produced locally next year, setting up future margin and cash benefits.

Portfolio Diversification Gains Traction

The core tonic range grew a modest 3%, but the broader portfolio rose 13% and now accounts for nearly half of group sales. Beyond-tonic products represent about a third of U.K. sales and over 40% in the rest of the world, demonstrating success in reducing reliance on tonic.

Priority Flavors Powering Growth

Five priority flavors now drive roughly half of group sales and delivered about 85% of first-half growth. Supported by targeted marketing and innovation, these products are increasingly consumed both in mixed drinks and as premium soft drinks, deepening Fever-Tree’s presence across occasions.

‘Straight Up or Mixed’ Campaign Success

In the U.K., the Straight Up or Mixed campaign reached around 11.5 million adults and boosted sales of featured flavors by 22%. The company is now adapting the campaign for France, Canada, Belgium and Australia, seeking to replicate its impact across other key markets.

U.K. Market Returns to Growth

U.K. revenue rose 3%, helped by the successful campaign and favorable summer weather. Off-trade performance was particularly robust, with a further 2% value-share gain, while Fever-Tree maintained its leading distribution footprint and share in the on-trade despite a tougher backdrop.

European and Rest-of-World Performance

Europe delivered 4% underlying year-on-year growth, led by strong ginger beer sales, with Fever-Tree capturing more than half of the category’s retail growth and holding nearly 40% value share. Rest-of-world revenue climbed 5%, with underlying growth slightly higher at 6%, reinforcing geographic diversification.

Innovation in Non-Alcoholic and Adult Soft Drinks

In the U.K., non-alcoholic ready-to-drink lines gained good distribution across major grocers, attracting younger consumers into the category. In Australia, Lemon, Lime & Bitters secured listings in Coles and Woolworths, supported by strong shelf visibility and early sales momentum.

Moderation Trend Creates New Value Pool

Management highlighted that about 25 million U.K. adults intend to moderate alcohol consumption, with roughly 70% of no-alcohol occasions featuring soft drinks or non-alcoholic options. The relevant U.K. value pool is estimated around GBP 700 million, larger than the entire mixed category today.

Asset-Light, Cash-Generative Model

Fever-Tree’s outsourced, capital-light operating model continues to throw off significant cash. This supports investment in marketing, innovation and potential deals while keeping the balance sheet strong and enabling surplus capital to be returned to shareholders.

Resilient Supply Chain and Cost Position

Supply-chain resilience improvements are helping the business navigate geopolitical volatility. Bottles and cans are materially hedged for energy costs through 2026–2028, while central costs have fallen as a percentage of adjusted revenue as technology investments are leveraged.

Medium-Term Profit Growth Ambitions

The group remains confident of delivering in line with expectations and sees U.S. revenue growth accelerating as the year progresses. Management pointed to consensus forecasts for around a 60% EBITDA uplift over the next two years, with much of the U.S. contribution backed by a profit guarantee.

Expected Free Cash Flow Expansion

Local U.S. production is expected to improve working capital from 2027, with the group targeting at least GBP 100 million of free cash flow across 2027 and 2028. Excess cash is earmarked for shareholder returns once growth investments have been funded.

U.S. Margin Pressure from Higher Marketing

U.S. EBITDA margins declined as anticipated, mainly due to heavier marketing spend to build the brand. Management expects incremental U.S. marketing investment to ease back to more typical levels over the medium term, supporting future margin recovery.

Challenges in U.K. On-Trade Channel

The company acknowledged ongoing challenges in the U.K. on-trade market, reflecting broader industry pressures. Even so, Fever-Tree retains a market-leading distribution footprint and share, positioning it well for any eventual recovery in on-premise demand.

EPR Levy Provision Hits Group Margin

Rest-of-group margin recovery took place despite a GBP 2.6 million provision for the 2026 U.K. on-trade EPR levy. Management noted the legal challenge has stalled since March, and said the provision is required under accounting standards, adding a temporary drag on profitability.

European Revenue Phasing to Reverse

While Europe posted 4% underlying growth, reported revenue in the first half benefited from favorable shipment phasing. Management cautioned that reported European revenue will be affected as these timing benefits unwind in subsequent periods.

Short-Term Earnings Drag from U.S. Investment

Executives framed 2025 as a transition year and 2026 as an investment year for the U.S. opportunity. The heavier spending and build-out are expected to dampen earnings in the near term, but are seen as critical to unlocking larger profits later.

Working Capital Improvement Pushed to 2027

Working capital stood around 20% in 2024 and eased to about 16.6% last year, but is expected to remain broadly at that level through 2026. Management said the next step-change should arrive in 2027 as U.S. production onshoring scales, releasing more cash.

U.S. Adult Soft Drinks Remain Longer-Term Play

Fever-Tree and Molson Coors see a significant opportunity in the growing U.S. adult soft-drinks segment. However, they agreed to focus the Molson Coors network on the core mixer business for the next couple of years, deferring broader category expansion for now.

Guidance Signals Profit Step-Change Ahead

Looking to FY 2026 and beyond, the group expects accelerating U.S. revenue growth, good underlying progress elsewhere, and some European reported revenue drag as phasing unwinds. Management guided group EBITDA margin up from around 12.5% this year to the high 14%–15% range, with a step-change in profitability and at least GBP 100 million of free cash flow projected across 2027 and 2028.

Fever-Tree’s call painted the picture of a fast-growing premium drinks brand investing heavily now to secure a larger global footprint and stronger profit base later. While short-term earnings will feel the weight of U.S. marketing and operational build-out, the combination of rising market share, portfolio diversification, strong cash generation and clear margin targets offers investors a compelling medium-term growth story.

data.title: HiTech raises $4m to fund Hudson acquisition and bolster balance sheet
data.description:
Hitech Group Australia Limited ( (AU:HIT) ) has provided an update.

HiTech Group Australia has secured firm commitments for a $4 million equity placement to new institutional and professional investors, issuing four million shares at $1.00 each to expand its shareholder base. The funds will support working capital needs arising from its recent acquisition of selected assets from Hudson Global Resources and provide scope for accelerated debt reduction, while preserving much of HiTech’s existing cash reserves.

The Hudson acquisition is described as transformational, creating a national recruitment and professional services platform with about $216 million in pro forma combined revenue and a broader customer base across government and private sectors. By strengthening its balance sheet and funding integration of Hudson, HiTech aims to enhance its growth trajectory, extend market reach and consolidate its position in Australia’s technology-focused recruitment and professional services industry.

data.title: Bunzl Earnings Call Highlights Growth, Resilience and Buyback
data.description:
Bunzl ((BZLFY)) has held its Q2 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Bunzl’s latest earnings call struck a distinctly upbeat tone, underscoring broad-based revenue and volume growth, stronger profitability and cash generation, and a recovering North American Distribution arm. Management paired this optimism with an upgraded 2026 outlook and a sizeable share buyback, while openly flagging that part of the margin strength stems from temporary inflation effects and that comparatives will get tougher in the second half.

Broad-Based Growth in Revenue and Volumes

Group revenue rose 4.1% at constant currency in the first half, with 3.2% underlying growth driven roughly two-thirds by higher volumes and one-third by pricing. Growth was delivered across all business areas, marking five straight quarters of underlying revenue expansion and an acceleration from 2% in Q1 to 4.3% in Q2.

Promotion

55% Off TipRanks

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Improved Profitability and Margin Expansion

Adjusted operating profit climbed 8% year-on-year to GBP 441 million, lifting the operating margin by 30 basis points to 7.3%. Management attributed the margin gain to the net impact of inflation, initial Nisbets synergies and stabilization in the Distribution business, while cautioning that some of these benefits are temporary.

Upgraded Outlook for 2026

On the back of the strong first-half performance, Bunzl raised its outlook for 2026, now expecting group operating margins to be broadly flat year-on-year. Adjusted operating profit is projected to show modest growth, signaling confidence that the current level of profitability can be sustained despite expected margin headwinds.

Robust Cash Generation and High Returns

Free cash flow increased 5.6% to GBP 328 million, with cash conversion at 90% when stripping out the tariff refund inflow. Return on invested capital reached 13.3% and return on average operating capital 38%, with management noting that returns were slightly higher in the first half than usual.

Balance Sheet Strength and Capital Allocation

Adjusted net debt to EBITDA stood at 1.8x, below the 2 to 2.5x target range and highlighting ample balance sheet capacity. Bunzl unveiled a GBP 500 million share buyback over the next 12 months while preserving headroom for bolt-on acquisitions, which remain the company’s top capital allocation priority.

Dividend Growth and Ongoing Acquisitions

The interim dividend was increased by 3%, with the company expecting a 2026 dividend cover of 2.4x. Bunzl has completed two acquisitions so far this year and reiterated that committed acquisition spending is likely to be higher in 2026 than in 2025 as deal flow normalizes.

North America Recovery and Distribution Strength

North America delivered 4.6% underlying revenue growth, supported by both volume and inflation. Within this, the Distribution business posted 8% underlying revenue growth, largely driven by volume, new business wins in late 2025 and strong grocery partnerships, with margins improving modestly.

Operational Turnaround in Distribution

Management said North America Distribution has regained agility and service quality, with on-time-in-full performance back to 2019 levels. Staff turnover has fallen meaningfully, sales-team engagement has improved and collaboration across functions has strengthened, underpinning the division’s recovery.

New Growth Initiatives in Distribution

Near-term priorities include appointing a new CEO for the Distribution segment and opening two coastal mixing centers. These facilities will hold imported products for regional distribution centers, aiming to improve product availability, enhance warehouse productivity and unlock fresh commercial opportunities with customers.

Continental Europe Growth and Efficiencies

Continental Europe achieved just over 2% underlying revenue growth, with momentum improving through the half on better volumes and higher selling prices. In France, Bunzl’s largest Cleaning & Hygiene business completed warehouse consolidation from 15 sites to 6, delivering higher service levels, lower inventory, more capacity and improved safety.

European Wins and adidas Safety Footwear Deal

Across Europe, Bunzl secured about EUR 30 million of annualized net new business in the first half. The company also highlighted a global exclusive license with adidas for safety footwear, initially launching in several European countries with scope to broaden the product range and expand into new markets.

Solid Profit Growth in the U.K. and Ireland

In the U.K. and Ireland, underlying revenue grew slightly, mainly on volumes, but profits advanced more strongly. Adjusted operating profit rose 9% and margins improved, helped by Nisbets synergies and a one-off property gain, which together offset ongoing overhead cost inflation.

Rest of World Revenue and Margin Upside

In the Rest of the World segment, revenue at constant currency grew 5%, predominantly driven by acquisitions, with almost 2% underlying growth also contributing. Operating profit surged by just over 15% as gross and operating margins expanded significantly, with Brazil highlighted as a notable outperformer.

Proven Acquisition Model and Pipeline

Bunzl has identified over 1,300 potential acquisition targets and continues to focus on bolt-ons. From 2020 to 2025, 74 of 77 deals were bolt-ons, averaging around GBP 25 million per transaction and GBP 300 million in annual bolt-on spend, purchased at roughly 8x operating profit and delivering a two-year ROIC of 13.3%.

Operational Efficiency and Digital Progress

The company completed 15 warehouse consolidations and relocations in the first half of 2026, reinforcing its efficiency drive. Digital orders have risen to 78% of total orders from 76% in 2025, and management said artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in sales, operations and support processes.

Resilient, Diversified Business Model

Bunzl emphasized its diversification across roughly 150 businesses, geographies and sectors, with exposure to essential products and strong cash generation. About half of group profit now comes from Safety, Health Care and Cleaning & Hygiene, which management sees as offering the strongest growth prospects and highest margins.

Managing Inflation While Protecting Volumes

The group said it has successfully navigated product and operating cost increases linked to geopolitical pressures. Tools included selective price increases, surcharges on fuel and freight, and ongoing efficiency measures, enabling Bunzl to maintain volume growth despite higher costs.

Temporary Inflation Tailwind Set to Fade

Management acknowledged that part of the first-half margin uplift was driven by inflation-related effects, including selling inventory bought at lower cost. Gross margin peaked in June and started to ease in July, and Bunzl expects this inventory benefit to unwind in the second half, putting downward pressure on margins.

Second-Half Margin Pressure Ahead

The company expects second-half margins to be lower year-on-year as temporary inflation gains reverse and selling prices are reduced in some areas. Non-repeat of first-half Nisbets synergies, annualization of late-2025 business wins and higher variable operating costs tied to better profit performance will also weigh on margin.

Higher Operating Costs and Cost Mix Shifts

The operating cost-to-sales ratio rose slightly to 22% from 21.8% at actual currency, reflecting fuel and freight inflation and higher variable costs, especially in North America. Wages and property costs were described as being at more normal levels, suggesting the main pressure is transport and performance-linked expense.

North America Profit Constraints and End-Market Issues

Despite top-line progress, North America’s operating profit was flat as inflation benefits were offset by a shift toward lower-margin grocery and higher variable costs. Retail, Mexico and convenience-store operations faced ongoing end-market challenges, with the convenience-store business suffering volume declines.

Return on Operating Capital Down in North America

Return on average operating capital in North America fell versus the prior year, when second-half 2024 profits were stronger. The current period was also affected by investment in working capital, demonstrating that the region’s recovery is still a work in progress despite better revenues.

Regional Headwinds Across Key Markets

France saw selling-price deflation partially offsetting volume growth, although this deflation is beginning to moderate. New Zealand was hit by reduced public health care spending, Asia Pacific suffered health care margin pressure, and safety revenues in the U.K. and Ireland declined after major infrastructure projects ended.

Tariff Refunds and Accounting Impacts

U.S. IEEPA tariff refunds reduced statutory revenue by 1.2%, with no effect on adjusted operating profit thanks to a matching cost-of-sales adjustment. Bunzl received a GBP 71 million cash inflow linked to these refunds and expects most of it to be repaid to customers in the second half, pending further clarification.

Working Capital and Cash Conversion

Excluding the tariff refund, cash conversion came in at 90%, which management described as slightly below usual due to working capital investment. Even so, this level remains aligned with Bunzl’s target and supports the company’s ability to fund growth and shareholder returns.

Acquisition Timing Uncertainty

Management noted that market uncertainty has led some business owners to delay sales, constraining deal flow over the past 18 months. Bunzl has spent less than GBP 150 million on acquisitions in the last 20 months, compared with a typical two-year spend near GBP 600 million, and warned that acquisition timing can be lumpy.

Tougher Comparatives and 2027 Visibility

The second half will face more demanding comparatives as major late-2025 business wins annualize, potentially dampening growth rates. Management also said exiting 2026 with volumes below intra-year levels could affect 2027 performance, but chose not to provide specific guidance for that year.

Guidance and Outlook for 2026

For 2026, Bunzl expects revenue growth at constant exchange rates, excluding U.S. tariff refunds, to be driven by modest underlying growth supplemented by some inflation and a small contribution from acquisitions.
